decision_rule: No intervention is recommended solely because it may raise births. It must improve reproductive freedom, parent and child wellbeing, distributional fairness and measurable security.

interventions.name: Childcare Reliability Guarantee
interventions.barrier: Unmet demand, closures, shortened hours and lack of backup care
interventions.mechanism: Guarantee a usable place, publish reliability metrics and provide backup when contracted care repeatedly fails.
interventions.evidence_state: strong problem evidence; intervention effect requires pilot evaluation
interventions.pilot: Compare participating and matched municipalities over 24 months, with pre-registered definitions and no fertility claim before adequate follow-up.

interventions.name: Equal-Care Parental Leave Test
interventions.barrier: Highly unequal leave duration and gendered career costs
interventions.mechanism: Test more non-transferable, adequately paid leave for each parent plus flexible phased return without lowering household security.
interventions.evidence_state: strong inequality evidence; design effects differ across income groups and require evaluation
interventions.pilot: Model distributional effects first, then test with employers or public-sector cohorts and compare by income and family form.

interventions.name: Family Housing Access Pilot
interventions.barrier: High housing costs and delayed access to adequate independent housing
interventions.mechanism: Offer transparent priority, guarantees or long-term affordable family units tied to need rather than a pronatalist payment.
interventions.evidence_state: strong housing-pressure context; direct fertility effect uncertain
interventions.pilot: Five-city comparison using common eligibility, waiting-time and counterfactual rules.

interventions.name: Automatic Family Benefits
interventions.barrier: Administrative burden, fragmented applications and unknown non-take-up
interventions.mechanism: Pre-fill or automatically grant eligible benefits where legally possible, with human review and multilingual explanations.
interventions.evidence_state: high plausibility; Germany-wide cross-benefit baseline missing
interventions.pilot: One-stop pilot covering a small set of benefits in two jurisdictions before national scaling.

interventions.name: Pregnancy and Parenthood Career Protection
interventions.barrier: Motherhood-related employment, earnings and promotion penalties
interventions.mechanism: Measure and reduce preventable parenthood penalties through predictable schedules, transparent promotion data, return pathways and enforcement.
interventions.evidence_state: strong gender-gap evidence; specific employer interventions require causal testing
interventions.pilot: Public-sector and volunteer-employer cohort with independent evaluation and anti-retaliation safeguards.

interventions.name: Reproductive Health Access Map
interventions.barrier: Unequal information, eligibility, cost and waiting times for fertility and reproductive healthcare
interventions.mechanism: Publish access rules, costs, waiting times and referral pathways; improve evidence-based counselling and equitable eligibility.
interventions.evidence_state: individual unmet-need relevance is clear; macro fertility impact is limited and should not be overstated
interventions.pilot: Public access map and patient-journey audit without collecting identifiable health records in SafeTrace.

interventions.name: Postpartum Security Standard
interventions.barrier: Fragmented physical and mental-health support after birth
interventions.mechanism: Define minimum follow-up, screening, referral and practical support after birth, including partner inclusion.
interventions.evidence_state: health and wellbeing rationale strong; Germany baseline and fertility link need mapping
interventions.pilot: Regional care-pathway audit using aggregated outcomes and independent clinical review.

interventions.name: Wanted Second and Third Child Study
interventions.barrier: Different barriers by parity are hidden inside one national fertility rate
interventions.mechanism: Separate first-child, second-child and third-or-later intentions and identify which security constraint changes at each stage.
interventions.evidence_state: BiB identifies declining higher-order births as important; intervention evidence remains incomplete
interventions.pilot: FReDA-compatible analysis and qualitative review, not a cash-bonus experiment.

do_not_prioritise_without_evidence: campaigns that shame childfree people or women
fertility targets detached from child and parent wellbeing
municipal rankings before definitions and case mix are comparable
claims that migration or family policy alone can solve demographic ageing
